headline: Sweden's far right blames its defeat on immigration
description: After recording their first setback since 1988, the Sweden Democrats have fueled a conspiratorial narrative, accusing the opposition of orchestrating a form of 'electoral great replacement' to prevent the right from winning the elections.

French fishermen block ports over fuel prices
description: With the price of diesel rising to near-record levels, linked to the US-Iran war, fishermen blocked the entrances to two Mediterranean ports and a petrol depot in protest, prompting the government to increase petrol subsidies for the sector.

headline: Russia's giant game of Monopoly to fund the war
description: 'The Putin System' (3/3). Ever since the full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, sweeping property redistribution has been underway in Russia. Most often, the state has seized assets from entrepreneurs deemed disloyal and resold them to Vladimir Putin's loyalists.

headline: France to host two table tennis World Cups, building on Olympics momentum and Lebrun brothers
description: The French Table Tennis Federation announced on Thursday that France will host the 2027 and 2028 editions of the sport's singles World Cup, first in Montpellier and then in Paris.

headline: 'For the US authorities, the Taliban are reliable partners'
description: Political scientist Olivier Roy explains why, a quarter of a century after the 2001 terrorist attacks, the US has no choice but to normalize its relations with the Taliban, who, at the time, protected Al-Qaeda and harbored it in Afghanistan.

headline: Eiffel Tower director faces turmoil after sidelining of female staff at request of Hindu delegation
description: The exclusion of female staff members during a visit by members of an ultra-conservative Hindu religious group, sparked a strike and two investigations. Above all, the incident exposed the underlying unease within the company that runs the Iron Lady: contested management, social tensions and a lack of effective political oversight.

headline: Restaurant bankruptcies surge across France as costs climb and customers spend less
description: Over 4,900 restaurant businesses have filed for insolvency since the start of the year, a 7% increase compared to the same period in 2025. An exceptionally hot summer failed to reverse the downward trend for the industry.
